visual.observation: A page labeled "eBay Customer Service" displays a phone number and instructs the viewer to call and provide a one-time passcode when prompted so the caller can be identified.
visual.context: Presented within a visible customer-support webpage branded eBay; whether the page and phone contact are officially operated is unclear from the sampled frames.
visual.potential_relevance: A claimed support identity is linked to a request to make contact and disclose a one-time passcode, creating a task-relevant identity-and-sensitive-information relationship for review.
visual.limitations: The frames do not establish who operates the page or phone number, whether anyone called or disclosed the code, what the code would authorize, or any resulting transaction or outcome.

visual_context_notes.observation: The visible interface contains customer-service navigation, order-help items, selling-fee information, and topic selections including returns, payment holds, and transaction cancellation.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it is a practical walkthrough for contacting eBay support through the eBay help page while logged in. It shows customer-service navigation, issue selection, a phone number, and an issue-specific passcode as part of that support process, while discussing access problems and inaccurate wait-time messaging rather than soliciting money, credentials, or participation in a financial scheme.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: The central content is an operational demonstration of navigating a support webpage, selecting a problem category, and obtaining contact information.
